Radix tokens sold during initial token sale are called eXRD and follow a price-based unlocking schedule. 

Once the token price reaches the below price levels, more of the purchased token supply is unlocked, and are claimed by participants of the token sale. 

The tokens will be unlocked once the Simple Moving Average (SMA) of the crosses the following price milestones:

On instantiation of the Radix Ledger (mainnet) in our Olympia release, the ERC-20 eXRD tokens will be exchangeable 1:1 for the new XRD token. 

The price based unlocking mechanism starting with the eXRD token will continue for the XRD token on the Radix Ledger. 

The new XRD token will be instantiated as locked tokens for: the founders, the remainder of the RADIX LEDGER Subsidy; the remainder of the Dev Incentives; the remainder reserved for endowment of the Radix Foundation; and an indefinitely locked allocation for the Stable Coin Reserve.

This chart shows the distribution as a percentage of the maximum 24 Billion supply. The tokens allocated to Network Emission will be distributed in equal parts to all valid delegators over a 40 year period for the release of mainet. 

Head over to our blog to find out more or read the Economic White Paper for full details. 

How many Radix tokens (eXRD) are available now?

The Circulating Supply can be found here.

The maximum supply is 24 billion XRD. 12 billion will exist at the launch of the network, where a large portion follows price vesting and 2.4 billion tokens are locked as a stable coin reserve. 

Yearly emission rewards will account for 300m eXRD tokens over 40 years, resulting in an additional 12 billion tokens. For more information, please see the Radix economic model here.
